// The positive control for `tests_hold_no_inert_loop`. One inert loop per
// keyword the scanner must still recognise — delete any of them and the guard
// reports "the scan proves nothing for those" instead of a clean workspace.

#[test]
fn a_table_the_strip_emptied() {
    let pairs = [(1, "a"), (2, "b")];
    assert_eq!(pairs.len(), 2);
    // WP-10's shape: the match arms moved to another crate and the body went
    // with them. The length assertion above kept this green.
    for (_expected, _kind) in pairs {}
}

// The strip one step further along: no loop left to find inert, and the name
// still promises the classification it no longer checks. Four of these reached
// `evelynn` under WP-10 and no gate in the repo saw them.
#[test]
fn a_body_the_strip_emptied_entirely() {}

#[test]
fn a_while_that_only_binds() {
    let cursor = 0;
    while cursor < 3 {
        let _step = cursor;
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_loop_with_nothing_left_in_it() {
    let budget = 3;
    loop {
        let _remaining = budget;
    }
}

// Neither of these is a violation — they sit here so the contrast is visible
// where the witness is read. A body that calls anything is exempt, and a
// `while` whose condition does the work is exempt with an empty body.
#[test]
fn a_loop_that_still_asserts() {
    for (expected, kind) in [(1, "a")] {
        assert_eq!(expected, kind.len());
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_drain_whose_condition_is_the_work() {
    while let Some(_finished) = tasks.join_next().await {}
}
